correctness.rationale: Rank-q character signature H_1 as set of colors, H_{q+1}(word)={ (c,H_q(prefix),H_q(suffix)) } is exactly the Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé q-round equivalence invariant by induction on initial chosen position, as in Mwesigye–Truss Theorem 1.2. Pure blue linear-order lengths are rank-3 equivalent after cap 7; EF equivalence preserved under word concatenation, so each of k+1 blue gaps can be capped independently and the 8^(k+1) finite tuples cover every infinite gap option. Independent character-signature enumeration (separately written from uploaded checker) over 512,4096,32768 tuples reproduced respectively 310/1865/11196 classes, sharp stratum-representative lengths 19/25/31, one extremal each and stated unique gap tuples. Only k=2 case excludes shorter representatives in the full binary language via rank-three control of red count; for k=3,4 claims strictly within same k.

value.rationale: The first three nontrivial minority-marker strata beyond the known one-red case give complete exact rank-three theory counts and extremal shortest-word data. Sparse markers are a motivated complexity regime for finite model theory; the cap-plus-signature method makes the values exhaustive and reusable, not random arbitrary strings.

final_claim: For binary linear orders with exactly k named-red occurrences, k=2,3,4 and variable blue gaps, rank-three first-order equivalence has respectively 310,1865,11196 classes; maximum within-stratum minimal lengths 19,25,31 with one extremal class whose canonical gap tuples are (6,5,6),(6,5,5,6),(6,5,5,5,6). Gaps can be capped at seven without changing rank-three theory.
limitations: Exactly k=2,3,4 red points in two-colour linearly ordered structures; q=3 only.
No claim of global optimal length for k>=3 across other red counts; no general all-k formula.
